nodes.line: You will have to speak up, the trains are in.

You are the first person to stop all morning. I am sending back 68 papers a day from Carlton and paying to have them collected, which is a business model somebody invented on purpose. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Take your time. Do not take a week.

Not being dramatic about this. They will drop my Carlton order if I can show $77 of turnover on the other side of the shop by every second Friday. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. Come and find me after, either way.
Take a breath. Then say the whole thing.

choices.text: The Better Rate, Carlton — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
I have got about four minutes before I am needed.

I am told you do odd jobs. I do the Carlton round from ten past five and for the last fortnight somebody has been taking the papers off the front steps behind me. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. Whatever you find, bring it to me first.

I'll be straight with you. There is a dog on the Carlton round that has had two of my bags and a milk crate that was not even mine. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. That's it. That's the whole ask.
Go on then. What did you find.

choices.text: The Dog on Ash Street, Carlton — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
Ah. Someone with two working legs.

It has been three weeks. Nine of us at Carlton have gone in on the same numbers since every second Friday and one of us has stopped putting money in. I am aware how that sounds. If it's nothing, it's nothing. Tell me anyway.

Nobody else has offered, so. The agency at Kogarah closed six months before Carlton started struggling, and I would very much like to know what they know. My wife says I should let it go. My wife is wrong. If anyone asks, you were never here.
You came back. That already puts you ahead.

choices.text: The Other Agency, Carlton — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
You are early. Or late. I have lost track.

You are the first person to stop all morning. There has been a car in the Lindfield yard since a Tuesday with a laminated notice on the passenger seat and no owner answering. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Take your time. Do not take a week.

Not being dramatic about this. Now that it is documented, Lindfield is owed $68 in storage and the only person who can pay it is the person not answering. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. Come and find me after, either way.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.

choices.text: The Unclaimed Falcon, Lindfield — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
Been here since before it was like this. Go on.

I am told you do odd jobs. I am in my first year at Lindfield and I have to log 27 hours on a job I am not allowed to touch on my own. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. Whatever you find, bring it to me first.

I'll be straight with you. Somebody has been coming into the Lindfield yard after two in the afternoon to use the air line, and last week they used the compressor as well. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. That's it. That's the whole ask.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.

choices.text: The Air Line, Lindfield — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Indira, the bloke whose car it is at Lindfield

nodes.line: Do not mind the mess. It is structural now.

It has been three weeks. My car has been at Lindfield since a Tuesday and every time I ring, the quote has grown by about $27. I am aware how that sounds. If it's nothing, it's nothing. Tell me anyway.

Nobody else has offered, so. The insurance assessor who signs off every job at Lindfield works out of Roseville, and he has never once seen the car he is assessing. My wife says I should let it go. My wife is wrong. If anyone asks, you were never here.
Well? I can read your face from here.

choices.text: My Own Car, Lindfield — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.

npcs.name: Kamila, shop manager at Bexley North

nodes.line: If you are selling something the answer is no.

You are the first person to stop all morning. People leave things at the Bexley North roller door after first light and by morning it is rained on and it is our problem and our tip fee. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Take your time. Do not take a week.

Not being dramatic about this. The photos worked, which means Bexley North can claim back the $68 we have paid to throw away other people's furniture since every second Friday. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. Come and find me after, either way.
Sit. Talk. Then I will decide how I feel.

choices.text: Dumped Out the Back, Bexley North — that's done.
The Tip Fee, Bexley North — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
Cash only and no, I am joking. What do you want.

I am told you do odd jobs. Something came into Bexley North on every second Friday in a box of paperbacks that I do not think the family meant to give away. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. Whatever you find, bring it to me first.

I'll be straight with you. Two people have been coming into the Bexley North sorting room since every second Friday and taking the good stock before it reaches the floor, and one of them volunteers here. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. That's it. That's the whole ask.
You have got that look. Good or bad, out with it.

choices.text: The Good Box, Bexley North — that's done.
Sorting Room, Bexley North — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.

npcs.name: Theo, volunteer driver at Bexley North

nodes.line: You have got a face like you can keep your mouth shut.

It has been three weeks. I do the Bexley North pick-ups in a van with 9 thousand on it and a door that only opens if you know about it. I am aware how that sounds. If it's nothing, it's nothing. Tell me anyway.

Nobody else has offered, so. Everything Bexley North cannot sell goes to a warehouse at Kingsgrove, and nobody there has ever answered a phone in my hearing. My wife says I should let it go. My wife is wrong. If anyone asks, you were never here.
Before you start: did anyone see you.

choices.text: The Van, Bexley North — that's done.
Head Office, Bexley North — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
